subject: scripts/falsify-timeseries.mjs
claim: The falsification harness survives a forced kill: a breakage applied when the process dies is recoverable from disk, the next run refuses to start rather than mutating an already-wrong file, and --recover restores the original bytes exactly.
whyThisWasRunAtAll: A harness that mutates real sources is itself a hazard. Its window is a whole verifier run, and one of its breakages unscopes the CSS rule that collapses every KaTeX radical -- so a kill during that case would silently reinstate wrong mathematics. Claiming crash safety from reading the code is not evidence; on Windows a forced kill delivers no catchable signal, so the signal handlers in the harness are a courtesy and the sidecar is the actual protection. This is that protection exercised.
method: Recorded the SHA-256 of all ten files any breakage can touch.
Started `node scripts/falsify-timeseries.mjs` as a detached process.

Confirmed mid-run that the lock file held the running PID and that a .timeseries-falsify-orig sidecar existed beside src/learn/data/timeseries-models.js, meaning a breakage was applied at that moment.
Terminated that PID with `taskkill /F`, which on Windows delivers no catchable signal and unwinds no stack.
Inspected the tree, then ran the harness again, then ran it with --recover, then re-compared every hash.

afterForcedKill.interpretation: The kill did leave a breakage applied. That is the hazard, and it is why the sidecar and the refusal-to-start exist rather than a signal handler.

secondRunRefusedToStart.message: scratch/timeseries-falsification.lock exists: another falsification run is in progress, or one was killed. Two instances mutating the same files is how a breakage was left on disk before.

afterRecoveryReruns.verify-timeseries-data.py: PASS, 6647 of 6659 leaves derived, module byte-identical
afterRecoveryReruns.falsify-timeseries.mjs: PASS, 23 of 23 breakages fired and named their guard

concurrencySafety: A sibling lesson's harness held scratch/formulation-falsification.lock throughout. This harness uses its own lock path and its own sidecar suffix, and its evidence snapshot is anchored to docs/teaching/evidence/timeseries-*.json and screenshots/timeseries-* only, so neither run could see or restore the other's artifacts.
limitations: This proves recovery from one kill at one point in one case. It is not a proof that every interleaving is recoverable -- a kill between writing the mutated file and flushing it, or a disk failure, is outside what any sidecar can promise.
The five browser breakages were not part of this test; they rebuild the site and were deferred to phase C.
Recovery restores SOURCE bytes. It does not re-run the verifiers, which is why --recover says so explicitly rather than implying the tree is trustworthy again.
